organizations.What they build: Provides GPU and Jetson computing plus the Isaac robotics stack. Isaac Sim simulates robots and sensors; Isaac Lab adds workflows for training robot policies, including reinforcement learning (learning through trial and reward).
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for a remote Isaac Lab tutorial or small compute allocation after publishing a reproducible demo; no sponsorship or free hardware is confirmed.

organizations.What they build: Develops the Optimus general-purpose humanoid program and AI for perception and robot control. Public program descriptions are not proof of unsupervised commercial deployment.
organizations._relationship_reason: A technical speaker is a more realistic request than access to a closed humanoid platform; approach through public robotics events, with no warm introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Builds and operates warehouse automation, including Proteus mobile robots, Sparrow picking arms and the tactile Vulcan system. Amazon's own fulfillment network provides a concrete customer and integration environment, unlike a staged home demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask an operations/robotics researcher to explain warehouse evaluation and failure recovery remotely. Robot access or a deployment partnership is unlikely for a new student lab.

organizations.What they build: Builds Spot for mobile inspection, Stretch for warehouse case handling, and Atlas for industrial humanoid work. These are different products and should not be treated as one general-purpose deployment.
organizations._relationship_reason: Request an engineering talk about integration and safety through a public event; purchasing or borrowing a robot is not assumed.

organizations.What they build: Builds robot-assisted surgical and bronchoscopy systems, including da Vinci. These assist trained clinical teams; they are not autonomous surgeons or appropriate beginner hardware.
organizations._relationship_reason: A talk on human control, validation and safety would broaden the lab beyond robot-learning demos. Clinical hardware access is not a realistic initial ask.

organizations.What they build: Builds Figure humanoids and Helix embodied AI. Its homepage presents Figure 03 for home assistance. In September 2025 it announced more than $1B of committed Series C capital at a $39B post-money valuation; committed funding is not revenue or evidence of deployment scale.
organizations._relationship_reason: Seek a researcher talk or public demo discussion, not hardware donation; the proprietary full-body platform is outside a small lab's practical scope.

organizations.What they build: Develops generalist robot policies in the pi family. A vision-language-action model turns camera images and instructions into robot actions. Its site provides pi0 code/weight releases and later models; Axios reported a $600M round in November 2025, but the opened article did not label its series.
organizations._relationship_reason: Publish a small-arm evaluation of released pi policies and ask for feedback or a remote paper discussion. This is more plausible than competing on foundation-model training scale.

organizations.What they build: Develops Skild Brain, a robot-control model intended to work across different robot bodies. Its January 2026 announcement reports $1.4B raised at a valuation above $14B; claims that it can control any robot remain company claims, not independently established guarantees.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask about cross-embodiment evaluation through a public research event. No open model or student-access program was established.

organizations.What they build: Builds Digit humanoids and Arc fleet software for industrial automation. Its September 2025 NVIDIA collaboration page confirms Series C investment and use of Isaac Lab for sim-to-real robot learning; its homepage identifies Salem as Digit's assembly location.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for a remote discussion of deployment metrics, recovery and simulation transfer; buying Digit is not assumed. Salem is the documented assembly site, not a verified legal HQ.

organizations.What they build: Builds Apollo humanoids for manufacturing and logistics. February 2026's company release reports more than $935M in total Series A financing and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz, GXO, Jabil and Google DeepMind. Apollo 2 is already in the pilot robot/model file and is not recreated here.
organizations._relationship_reason: Request a talk about humanoid manipulation and industrial pilots; a student hardware partnership is speculative, not an existing offer.

organizations.City: San Carlos, California (current about page); Palo Alto HQ announced in 2025
organizations.What they build: Develops NEO home humanoids. Norwegian origins do not exclude it: a July 2025 announcement established a US global HQ, while the current about page says San Carlos. Its last opened explicitly labeled financing is a $100M Series B announcement in January 2024, not a verified latest round.
organizations._relationship_reason: Seek a discussion of household data collection, remote assistance and privacy. Do not assume the lab can acquire or safely operate a home humanoid.

organizations.What they build: Builds Field Foundation Models: robot-control software designed to account for uncertainty and physical constraints in unstructured environments. Its August 2025 release reports $405M across two rounds and industrial deployments; Series B labeling comes from an opened secondary funding table.
organizations._relationship_reason: A talk contrasting risk-aware field autonomy with tabletop VLAs would test our wedge. Access to proprietary models and customer sites is unknown.

organizations.What they build: Connects university researchers and industry around domestic, medical, field and workplace robotics. Stanford's Mobile ALOHA project demonstrates learning mobile two-arm tasks from human demonstrations; the center itself also releases OpenSAI.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public Mobile ALOHA project and center seminars are cold outreach routes, not warm introductions
organizations._relationship_reason: Start with open project reproductions and a concise request to the relevant student authors. Formal industrial-affiliate access is not assumed.

organizations.What they build: UC Berkeley's AI research community includes robot learning. Berkeley's HIL-SERL uses demonstrations, a learned success classifier and human interventions to improve manipulation policies through reinforcement learning. The earlier SERL project is explicitly deprecated in favor of HIL-SERL.
organizations._relationship_reason: Reproduce a simulation baseline or analyze interventions and ask the authors for feedback; do not assume industrial arms are low-cost or safe without supervision.

organizations.What they build: University robotics institute spanning robotics research and education. Its homepage describes the Robotics Innovation Center in Pittsburgh. Specific robot/model attribution was not established from the opened institute page and is left unknown rather than inferred from unrelated projects.
organizations._relationship_reason: Approach public seminar speakers with a reproducible student demo and specific technical question. No warm introduction or formal partnership was found.

organizations.What they build: Toyota's US research organization studies mobile manipulation, human-robot interfaces and data collection for useful tasks. It leads core development of Drake, a tool for simulating dynamics and designing robot controllers. Parent Toyota is Japanese; this row is the US institute, not Toyota globally.
organizations._relationship_reason: Contribute a small Drake example or reproduce a published method, then ask for technical feedback. Corporate funding or robot access is not promised.

organizations.What they build: University represented here as the School type, with robotics research in CSAIL. Its Robot Locomotion Group originated Drake; core development is now led by TRI, so attributing Drake solely to MIT would be misleading.
organizations._relationship_reason: Use public Drake tutorials and ask a lab author for a remote reading-group talk. Admission, lab access and institutional affiliation are not implied.

organizations.What they build: Independent robotics hub supporting commercialization, with startup workspace, prototyping, testing and connections among startups, academia and industry. It does not itself imply a named production robot or AI model.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for an ecosystem-introduction call or remote startup panel. Physical workspace and resident benefits require separate eligibility and a Boston presence.

organizations.What they build: US nonprofit robotics industry association connecting companies, universities and investors. Its 2026 prospectus documents meetups, investor summits and hackathons, including the 2025 LeRobot Global Hackathon.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; prospectus lists managing director Andra Keay as a public contact, not a warm introduction
organizations._relationship_reason: Propose a remote cross-community demo exchange or a future joint low-cost robotics hackathon. The documented hackathon history is relevant, but no 42AI partnership exists.

organizations.What they build: US nonprofit steward of open robotics software under the Open Robotics brand. OSRA provides governance and community participation for ROS, Gazebo and Open-RMF. OSRF is distinct from the commercial subsidiaries acquired by Intrinsic in 2022; ROS 2 already exists in the pilots.
organizations._relationship_reason: Contribute documentation, examples or bug fixes before requesting a community speaker. Paid OSRA membership is not required to begin learning or contributing.

organizations.What they build: Deep-tech investor whose opened portfolio and 2025 report include Physical Intelligence, Anduril and Auris Health. Provides capital and company-building support rather than a lab-owned robot platform.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for a robotics market-feedback session after a clear demo; startup equity investment is not a realistic funding plan for a student association.

organizations.What they build: Deep-tech venture firm with documented investment in Agility Robotics since 2020 and a portfolio page discussing warehouse humanoids. Its robotics relevance is grounded in an opened investment page, not a claim to be the most active investor by deal count.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for feedback on deployment economics through a public event or cold outreach. Do not frame a student lab as an investable startup without a commercial plan.

organizations.What they build: The 2026 US edition of the international robot-learning conference, November 9–12 in Austin. Combines research papers, demonstrations and workshops at the intersection of machine learning and robotics; this row is the US edition, not a permanently US-based organization.
organizations._relationship_reason: Use open papers and streamed talks, contact workshop authors, and consider a later reproducible-demo submission. Travel and acceptance are not assumed.

organizations.What they build: US robotics and automation trade show connecting component vendors, integrators and customers. The opened homepage has rolled forward to May 10–13, 2027 in Las Vegas and links a 2026 recap; no claim is made that the 2026 edition was in Las Vegas.
organizations._relationship_reason: Use exhibitor conversations to learn integration economics and identify suppliers for later outreach. Exhibitor attendance is not sponsorship of our lab.

organizations.What they build: Boston engineering-focused robotics event. The opened 2026 page lists speakers from Open Robotics, PickNik, Universal Robots and other builders, making it useful for systems engineering beyond foundation-model headlines.
organizations._relationship_reason: Approach a relevant listed speaker for a remote technical session; use public material before committing to transatlantic travel.

robots_models.Name: NVIDIA Isaac Lab
robots_models.Price / access: Public framework; GPU/compute costs depend on experiment.
robots_models.Key specs: Robot-learning workflows on Isaac Sim, including reinforcement learning and learning from demonstrations.
robots_models.Why it matters: A sim-to-real entry point, but simulator success is not proof of real-world robustness.

robots_models.Name: Tesla Optimus
robots_models.Price / access: Closed development program; student access and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Bipedal humanoid program requiring balance, navigation, perception and manipulation.
robots_models.Why it matters: High-profile reference for full-system integration, not a practical starter platform.

robots_models.Name: Amazon Proteus
robots_models.Price / access: Internal Amazon deployment; external purchase price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Autonomous mobile robot designed to move heavy carts and avoid obstacles; the next generation was described as being piloted.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows that navigation, operations and workflow fit matter as much as model novelty.

robots_models.Name: Amazon Vulcan
robots_models.Price / access: Internal fulfillment technology; price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Picking/stowing system using tactile feedback to detect contact and regulate applied force.
robots_models.Why it matters: Introduces force sensing and manipulation beyond RGB-camera-only imitation.

robots_models.Name: Spot (Boston Dynamics)
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial platform; price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Mobile inspection robot for gathering data in work environments.
robots_models.Why it matters: A field-robotics comparison point; hardware cost and safe deployment differ from small arms.

robots_models.Name: Stretch (Boston Dynamics)
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial warehouse system; price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Robot for case handling and warehouse automation.
robots_models.Why it matters: A concrete, task-focused alternative to general-purpose humanoids.

robots_models.Name: Atlas (Boston Dynamics)
robots_models.Price / access: Industrial humanoid program; student access and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Atlas is presented as an industrial humanoid; not the unrelated microagi Atlas model in the Europe pilot.
robots_models.Why it matters: Separates impressive locomotion and industrial integration from an affordable student platform.

robots_models.Name: da Vinci 5
robots_models.Price / access: Clinical system for trained physicians; price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Robot-assisted multiport surgical system with instruments, imaging and surgeon control.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows why safety, human oversight and regulated deployment cannot be replaced by a compelling learning demo.

robots_models.Name: Figure 03
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial availability and price unknown from opened pages.
robots_models.Key specs: General-purpose humanoid presented for everyday home tasks, using Helix AI.
robots_models.Why it matters: A closed full-stack comparison point; household marketing is not measured autonomous reliability.

robots_models.Name: Helix (Figure)
robots_models.Price / access: Proprietary; model access and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Embodied-intelligence system used by Figure for perception and control in changing home environments; precise public architecture not established here.
robots_models.Why it matters: Useful contrast with downloadable pi-family models. Policy classification is broad; no exact VLA architecture is inferred.

robots_models.Name: pi0 (Physical Intelligence)
robots_models.Price / access: Public code and checkpoints via openpi; check checkpoint-specific terms and GPU requirements.
robots_models.Key specs: Flow-based vision-language-action policy trained across robot tasks and bodies. Paper announced October 2024; public code/weights release followed in February 2025.
robots_models.Why it matters: An accessible baseline for adaptation experiments; a pretrained policy may fail on a different robot or camera setup.

robots_models.Name: pi0.5 (Physical Intelligence)
robots_models.Price / access: Public checkpoints and fine-tuning/inference examples in openpi; compute is not free.
robots_models.Key specs: Generalist VLA extending pi0 for open-world generalization; openpi documents the supported flow-matching head.
robots_models.Why it matters: Test transfer instead of assuming it: the repository explicitly warns that task checkpoints may not generalize to a new setup.

robots_models.Name: Skild Brain
robots_models.Price / access: Proprietary; public weights, student access and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Unified robot-control model intended for arms, mobile manipulators, quadrupeds and humanoids; generality is a company claim.
robots_models.Why it matters: Frames cross-embodiment transfer as a research goal, not a solved property of all robot policies.

robots_models.Name: Digit (Agility Robotics)
robots_models.Price / access: Industrial deployment discussions; price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Humanoid for repetitive industrial tasks, paired with Arc cloud fleet software.
robots_models.Why it matters: Illustrates deployment, fleet operations and simulation transfer beyond a single filmed demo.

robots_models.Name: NEO (1X Technologies)
robots_models.Price / access: Home robot / early-access program; current price and eligibility unknown from opened pages.
robots_models.Key specs: Home-focused humanoid with multiple development versions; the about page distinguishes NEO Beta/Gamma from EVE Industrial.
robots_models.Why it matters: A reference for domestic interaction and data collection, not evidence that a student lab should buy a humanoid.

robots_models.Name: Field Foundation Models (FieldAI)
robots_models.Price / access: Proprietary deployment platform; price and student access unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Physics-first, risk-aware autonomy models controlling multiple robot forms in unstructured environments. Exact model architecture and benchmark comparability are unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Tests whether robust field autonomy requires capabilities beyond inexpensive tabletop imitation.

robots_models.Name: Mobile ALOHA
robots_models.Price / access: Open research code; full hardware cost unknown here and not assumed to be SO-101-level.
robots_models.Key specs: Two-arm mobile teleoperation and imitation-learning platform. The paper reports co-training with static ALOHA data and 50 demonstrations per task; this does not guarantee the same result on other hardware.
robots_models.Why it matters: Strong reproduction reference that also exposes hardware, data-collection and recovery costs.

robots_models.Name: HIL-SERL
robots_models.Price / access: Public research implementation; physical arm, safety supervision and compute costs separate.
robots_models.Key specs: Human-in-the-loop reinforcement-learning system using reward classifiers, demonstrations and online interventions; succeeds the deprecated SERL implementation.
robots_models.Why it matters: A concrete way to compare demonstration-only learning against iterative correction.

robots_models.Name: Drake
robots_models.Price / access: Public C++/Python library with tutorials; check the repository license.
robots_models.Key specs: Dynamics simulation, planning and optimization-based control; originated at MIT CSAIL, core development now led by TRI.
robots_models.Why it matters: Provides a model-based baseline to compare against learned policies, avoiding an AI-only curriculum.

robots_models.Name: Gazebo
robots_models.Price / access: Open-source simulator; free public documentation.
robots_models.Key specs: Robot simulation with a physics server, GUI and SDF world/robot descriptions; OSRA governs the project under OSRF stewardship.
robots_models.Why it matters: A general robotics simulation alternative to a GPU-heavy robot-learning stack.

summary: NVIDIA supplies enabling compute and simulation; Amazon, Boston Dynamics and Intuitive show deployed systems, while Stanford, Berkeley, CMU, MIT and TRI anchor research.
Large disclosed rounds concentrate in humanoids and general robot intelligence: Figure reports >$1B committed Series C, Skild $1.4B, and Apptronik >$935M total Series A.
Concrete demand is visible in warehouse handling, industrial inspection/manufacturing and robot-assisted medicine; home humanoids remain a higher-uncertainty bet.
For a 15-student Paris lab, start with open policies/tools, publish a measured small-arm demo, and seek remote author feedback and community links through Open Robotics and Silicon Valley Robotics.

Low-cost robot learning is a credible learning and visibility wedge, not yet a proven business moat: test robustness, data cost and recovery against scripted baselines before scaling to expensive humanoids.
